context:
Duplication is a symptom, not the disease. For each cluster:
  1. Read both copies end-to-end. If they diverge meaningfully (different
     error handling, different SDK quirks), leave them alone and document
     in duplication-residuals.md.
  2. If they are genuinely identical in intent, extract a helper at the
     narrowest natural scope (module private helper > package mixin >
     cross-package utility).
  3. Write a unit test covering the extracted helper BEFORE migration.
  4. Migrate callers one at a time; commit per migration; run full
     platform tests.

For the apply_platform_optimizations cluster, coordinate with
quality-map-adapter-base-refactor-scope - if the adapter base is about
to grow a tuning module, that is the right destination. Do not extract
to a third location.
description:
Quality plan supplement - duplication workstream. pylint
`duplicate-code --min-similarity-lines=8` finds ~368 duplicate blocks in
benchbox/core/ and ~188 in benchbox/platforms/. Even at 15-line similarity,
100 blocks remain in platforms alone. Duplication across 73 adapters is
exactly what widens the blast radius of the adapter-base refactor and of
any future cross-cutting change (error capture, timing, validation).

Concrete clusters confirmed by inventory:
  - Azure fabric_spark_adapter ↔ synapse_spark_adapter (credential +
    token refresh logic, ~16 lines)
  - GCP dataproc_adapter ↔ dataproc_serverless_adapter (GCS path
    parsing + config validation, ~13 lines)
  - Databend ↔ Databricks (apply_platform_optimizations /
    apply_table_tunings dispatch pattern, ~20 lines)

Extract shared helpers where the duplication is genuine (same intent,
same behavior). Reject DRY where platforms diverge in meaningful ways -
the goal is fewer accidental copies, not forced abstraction.

Should run BEFORE quality-refactor-adapter-base-into-cohesive-modules so
the base refactor operates on deduplicated callers.

anti_patterns.why: hitting a duplicate-block count by splitting helpers into micro-functions is worse than the duplication

anti_patterns.dont: create cross-package utility modules for platform-specific helpers
anti_patterns.instead: keep helpers close to their platform

anti_patterns.dont: extract an abstraction that collapses meaningful platform differences
anti_patterns.why: false DRY hurts more than duplication

anti_patterns.dont: promote R0801 to error in this TODO
anti_patterns.instead: warn-only initially, promote in a follow-up

preserves.behavior: All platform tests pass after every slice
Lazy-loading and optional-dependency semantics preserved (helpers don't force-import SDKs at module load)
Platform-specific variants remain distinct where they genuinely differ (e.g., Fabric vs Synapse token scopes)
Runtime behavior of every affected adapter unchanged - this is structural consolidation, not behavior change

scope_rules.path_glob: adapter files not surfaced by the inventory

verifications.command: uv run --with pylint --with pandas --with polars pylint --disable=all --enable=duplicate-code --min-similarity-lines=15 benchbox/ 2>&1 | grep -cE 'R0801: Similar lines' || true
verifications.description: Cluster pair count drops materially from w1 baseline (~110)
verifications.expected: ≤ 102 (post-w5 baseline). The original ≤50 stretch goal is blocked by the R-06/R-08/R-09 refactors documented in docs/development/duplication-residuals.md; revisit after those land.

verifications.command: uv run -- pre-commit run duplicate-code --all-files || true
verifications.description: R0801 pre-commit hook is wired as warn-only
verifications.expected: hook runs; warnings printed; exit code acceptable per warn-only contract
